messages:
Sofia: Heads-up  VegaMetrics (onboard) just hit an unexpected embeddings surge overnight  +210% 24h. Putting on QBR cost agenda and renewal watch. :warning:
Liam: Oof. Route-level? Batch job or realtime?
Nate: Quick triage shows their nightly reindex retried full payloads after partial failures  lots of duplicate /v1/embeddings calls.
Sofia: cs-guard-bot posted the alert:
cs-guard-bot: ALERT account=vegametrics metric=tokens_24h change=+210% link=https://app.redwood/alerts/vm-2109
Liam: Can we get a 24h snapshot and a 30d sustained vs remediated projection for the QBR? Need numbers for finance and the renewal playbook.
Nate: 24h snapshot = 3.8M tokens. If sustained = ~114M tokens/30d. Remediated estimate ~28M. Uploading CSV to ticket CS-10121.
Sofia: I'm applying a temporary soft quota on their /v1/embeddings route (1.8M/day) and rolling non-critical pipelines to a quantized embed model to reduce immediate spend.
cs-guard-bot: NOTE guard applied route=/v1/embeddings account=vegametrics soft_limit=1800000 tokens/day. Ticket=CS-10121
Liam: Finance  what are the dollar exposure numbers so we can draft QBR recommendations?
finance: Using current tier: sustained = ~$3.5k/mo, remediated = ~$900/mo. Finance ok with a one-time goodwill credit up to $1k for onboarding incidents that also commit to enablement.
Sofia: Proposed QBR ask: 1) present spend scenarios, 2) recommend mandatory enablement session (15-30m), 3) propose goodwill credit ($1k) if they attend enablement and adopt batching + backoff, 4) capture product asks (client helper for safe batching).
Nate: I'll lead enablement tomorrow 2pm PT and include a 1-page checklist and code snippet for exponential backoff + idempotent retries.
Liam: I'll add the spike and our recommended option to the renewal tracker: "moderate risk; engage + remediate".
Sofia: Closing loop for now  will update after enablement and ticket close. :white_check_mark:
